title: Pinot Gris
description: Also called Pinot Grigio in Italy and Grauburgunder in Germany. One grape, from light and crisp to rich and spicy.
L: Explain its link to Pinot Noir

Pinot Gris gives white wines with pear, apple, white peach, lemon and, in richer styles, honey, spice and smoke. Acidity ranges from fresh to moderate, body from light to full. Its pinkish-grey skins can give a coppery tint. It's one of the world's most popular white grapes.

Pinot Gris is a colour mutation of Pinot Noir: the same DNA, but with less pigment in the skin, which is greyish-pink. Gris means grey in French; Grigio in Italian. It ripens early and reaches high sugar, so it can give fairly high alcohol, with lowish acidity if picked late.
Grey-pink skin, a Pinot Noir mutation
A colour mutation of Pinot Noir
A cross of Riesling and Chardonnay
It shares Pinot Noir's DNA, with lighter skin.

Light Pinot Grigio is pale, with neutral apple and lemon and crisp acidity. Richer Pinot Gris is deeper lemon or slightly copper, with pear, spice and honey, and a fuller, oilier texture. If you see a faint pink tint in a white, consider Pinot Gris.
Pale and crisp, or rich and spicy
Yes. That's why Gris, grey, is in its name.
Pinot Gris gives pear, apple and, when rich, spice and honey
It's a colour mutation of Pinot Noir
Its pink-grey skins can tint the wine
Explain how climate and yield shape it

Italy is the largest producer, mostly in the north-east: Veneto, Friuli and Alto Adige. Alsace makes its richest versions. Germany calls it Grauburgunder, for dry styles, or Ruländer, for sweeter ones. Oregon, New Zealand, Australia and Hungary, where it's Szürkebarát, grow it too.

The style depends heavily on yield and picking time. High yields and early picking give light, neutral, crisp wine. Low yields and later picking give concentrated, rich, spicy wines with more alcohol. The grape itself is the same; the grower's choices make the difference.
Match each name to its country.

In Italy, the Delle Venezie DOC, created in 2017, covers Pinot Grigio from Veneto, Friuli and Trentino, the world's largest Pinot Grigio appellation. It aimed to raise quality and control the huge volume produced for export. Alto Adige and Collio make more serious examples.
What gives a richer, spicier Pinot Gris?
High yields and early picking give the light, neutral style.
Italy makes the most; Alsace the richest
Yield and picking time decide the style
Delle Venezie DOC covers Italy's huge Pinot Grigio output
Explain what Pinot Grigio usually means
Explain what Pinot Gris usually means

Pinot Grigio, in the Italian style, is light-bodied, crisp and neutral, with lemon, green apple and almond. It's usually picked early, fermented cool in steel and bottled young. Its simplicity and freshness made it one of the best-selling white wines in the UK and US. Producers elsewhere use the name to signal this style.

Pinot Gris, in the Alsace style, is fuller and richer, with ripe pear, honey, ginger, smoke and spice, sometimes off-dry. It's picked riper, often from low-yield sites. Alsace's dry, sunny autumns and Grand Cru vineyards give some of the most concentrated versions. Oregon and New Zealand often use the name for richer styles.
A New Zealand label says Pinot Gris rather than Pinot Grigio. What does it most likely signal?
Producers use Gris to signal the fuller Alsace style.
When choosing, read the name as a style guide: Grigio for a light aperitif, Gris for a fuller wine with food.
Alsace Pinot Gris can be off-dry.
Yes. Ripe Alsace Pinot Gris sometimes has some residual sugar.
Pinot Grigio means light, crisp and neutral
Pinot Gris means rich, spicy and riper
Alsace makes the most concentrated Pinot Gris

Ramato means copper-coloured in Italian. It's a traditional style of Pinot Grigio from Friuli and Veneto, made with skin contact. Because Pinot Gris has pink-grey skins, leaving the juice on them for hours or days gives a copper or salmon hue, plus more body, texture and flavour.

Ramato was traditional in the Republic of Venice, where Pinot Grigio was made this way. Modern, pale Pinot Grigio, pressed quickly, became popular from the 1960s. Since the 2000s, producers have revived ramato, sometimes with longer skin contact, linking it to the orange wine movement.
Why does ramato have a copper colour?
Skin contact with Pinot Gris' pink-grey skins
The skins' pigment tints the juice.

Ramato is fuller and more textured than standard Pinot Grigio, with red apple, peach, dried herbs, and a light tannic grip. It's dry, and works well with food. Its colour sits between rosé and orange wine.
Ramato is copper-coloured Pinot Grigio made with skin contact
It's a Venetian tradition revived since the 2000s
It's fuller and more textured than standard Pinot Grigio
Know how long to keep it

Light Pinot Grigio suits aperitifs, salads, light seafood and simple pasta. Rich Pinot Gris suits roast pork, chicken, smoked fish, mushroom dishes and mildly spiced Asian food. Ramato suits charcuterie, risotto and grilled fish. Off-dry Alsace Pinot Gris suits foie gras.
Grigio light; Gris with richer food

Serve Pinot Grigio at 7 to 9 degrees, Pinot Gris and ramato at 10 to 12. Most Pinot Grigio is best within a year or two. Alsace Grand Cru Pinot Gris can age 10 years or more, developing honey and smoke.
Grigio young; Grand Cru Gris ages
Which dish suits a rich Alsace Pinot Gris?
Rich Pinot Gris matches pork and fruit.
An off-dry Alsace Pinot Gris with smoked salmon or a lightly spiced Thai dish brings out its ginger and smoky notes.
Most Pinot Grigio is made for long ageing.
Not true. It's best young and fresh.
Pinot Grigio suits light food; Pinot Gris richer dishes
Grand Cru Pinot Gris can age 10 years or more
